title: U.S. House · Rhode Island's 1st District
area: Providence, Pawtucket, Central Falls, East Providence, Cranston (part), and Rhode Island's northeastern communities.

context.text: Incumbent Gabe Amo (D) won the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed (52,446 votes). Kellie Keenan won the Republican primary unopposed. Pedro Soares de Souza is running as an independent; Wilfred Curioso (independent) did not make the ballot. Cook Political Report rates this district D+12.

summary.text: Gabe Amo is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Rhode Island's 1st District. He is a former Biden White House and Rhode Island state government official first elected to Congress in 2023.

background.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, in 1987; graduated from Moses Brown School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Wheaton College.
Served as special assistant and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs under President Joe Biden.
Worked as a states-strategy and program advisor on Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign, and as director of public engagement and community affairs for then-Rhode Island Governor Gina Raimondo.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, the House Committee on the Budget, and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

summary.text: Kellie Keenan is the Republican nominee for Rhode Island's 1st District. She is a public-health professional and small-business owner running on infrastructure and permitting reform, healthcare access, and lowering housing and energy costs.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Boston Latin School and an advanced certificate in public health management from Suffolk University.
Has worked more than a decade in healthcare and community health operations, including with Community Health Centers and federally funded programs.
Describes herself as a wife, mother of three daughters, and small business owner.

priorities.text: Infrastructure modernization and permitting reform, saying government red tape drives up costs and delays projects.
Strengthening Community Health Centers and expanding access to primary care and the healthcare workforce.
Lowering energy and housing costs through an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy and expanded housing development, particularly starter homes and small multifamily housing.

positions.summary: Supports permitting reform and reduced regulation to expand housing development, particularly starter homes and small multifamily housing.
Says she will advocate for policies that strengthen Community Health Centers and expand access to affordable, high-quality primary care.
